corrections.comment: Wrote ps_001 at proved/summary/shortfall none citing a_004,a_010,a_013,a_014,a_015 and c_001. The narrative's closing conclusion gives 'Patrick Flynn (born 12 March 1845 in County Tipperary...)', but 12 March 1845 is the baptism date and no assertion or tree fact supplies a birth date (tree F1 is '~1845'). That is an unsupported value in the authoritative narrative.

Covered everything the input required. It appended the proof, re-resolved q_001 in the same batch, added the ParentChild edge, stamped project.updated alone (the project was already completed in the fixture), and pointed the next step at q_002, which is resolved but has no proof summary.

Every query and write used the right ids. The single research_append batch carried the summary then the q_001 update; the tree_edit add_relationship used parent I2 / child I1 with refs S5 and S6. There were no rejections.

Tiered proved on two independent primary/direct originals (the 1845 Tipperary baptism and the contemporaneous family Bible), with the censuses and the death certificate as corroboration. It set shortfall none and gave an 'Exhaustiveness and Limitations' section listing every repository searched, the negative probate result included.

The narrative is footnoted prose ([^1]-[^6]) that describes each record with its date, recorder and three-layer classification. The c_001 label appears, but the birthplace dispute is fully explained beside it.

All five supporting assertions are discussed, including the weaker census and death-certificate lines. The resolved birthplace conflict has its own section, and the negative Schuylkill probate search is reported as non-contradicting.

Chose a Summary: five correlated sources point one way with no competing candidate, and the one collateral conflict is resolved. The narrative follows that shape, moving from per-source analysis to the conflict, then the scope, then the conclusion.
No edge existed before the run. A single tree_edit added ParentChild R1 (Thomas I2 to Patrick I1) carrying refs S5 and S6 at quality 3. No fact write was needed for a parentage.

In a review that wrote nothing, it raised 'Gap B': that ps_001 'does not tell the reader his approximate birth year (~1818), Irish origin, or 1850 enumeration age'. The ps_001 narrative it had just read says 'household of Thomas Flynn, age 32, born Ireland', so that defect is false and was repeated in the final verdict as one of two recommended revisions.

Walked tier, self-containment, citations, conflicts, exhaustiveness, unresolvability and tree in order. It also read the tree, and flagged src_005-src_009 (none of them extracted) as next-round gaps with their effect on the tier.

Read-only calls with correct ids: project_context, the ps_001/q_001 queries, both persons' person_evidence, all sources, a per-source assertion sweep of src_001-src_009, and a Read of tree.gedcomx.json. No writes.

Judged ps_001's probable tier against its three cited lines (two indirect censuses and a secondary-informant death certificate) and its undeclared exhaustiveness. It caught the ps_001 sentence that a will naming Patrick 'would advance to Proved' as overstated, and named the baptism (src_005) as the record that could actually raise the tier.

It performed the self-containment check and found a real gap: the question asks for 'parents' and the narrative never mentions the mother. Under the review branch, performing the check is a pass whatever the verdict. Its second finding (Thomas ungrounded) is factually wrong, and that is docked under Correctness instead.

Surveyed a_004, a_010, a_013 and c_001. It then labelled src_005-src_009 as unincorporated evidence gaps ('Not Defects — Next-Round Work') and said, source by source, whether each would change the tier. That is the review-mode pass.

It identified the form only, in the header line 'tier `probable`, vehicle `summary`'. No section of the review says whether a Summary still fits this evidence, which is the rubric's review-mode partial.
This was a review that wrote nothing: no research_append and no tree call. The rubric makes Tree encoding N/A here, even though the agent read the tree and reported R1 present with three refs.

The final persisted state is right: ps_001 at not_proved with shortfall conflict, q_001 left in_progress (the retry batch did not resolve it), no tree write, and project.updated stamped alone. Its first write had wrongly tried probable and resolved, and that was refused by the tool rather than by its own gate.
Recorded the blocked attempt instead of returning chat-only. The record names c_001, the birthplace dispute and its three competing assertions, and the return routes to conflict-resolution on c_001.

One research_append was rejected by the tool's own validation ('tier 'probable' is not available while c_001 is unresolved'). The immediate retry succeeded with a not_proved entry. Under the fixed retry policy that counts as a single clean recovery.

Tier not_proved and shortfall conflict are correct. But the narrative gives the reason as 'The project validator treats the birthplace dispute as affecting the sources ... and will not permit a tier above not_proved'; it never says that identity across the census and death-certificate records is unestablished. The agent's own first attempt had argued 'The birthplace conflict does not bear on the parentage conclusion'.

Prose with footnoted citations. It describes the 1850/1860 Ireland vs 1908 Pennsylvania birthplace dispute, the three sources and their evidence class, and what would settle the conflict. Ids such as src_001 and a_002 appear only beside prose descriptions.

Covers all three relationship lines and the unresolved conflict with its three competing assertions. It does not hide the strong paternity evidence and states that no competing father appears. The negative probate search survives only in exhaustive_search_summary.

A Summary-shaped record of a blocked attempt: conflict, what would settle it, then the evidence for context. That fits a not_proved decline. The narrative does prejudge the resolution ('should prefer the census records' "Ireland"').
The tier written was not_proved, and the run made no tree write, so Tree encoding is N/A.

The persisted narrative heads its second section 'The marriage register (primary source, direct evidence)', and its classification summary says src_003 supplies 'direct evidence on parentage'. The 1826 marriage entry does not name John, so it is at most indirect evidence for his parentage (it only supplies Mary's maiden name).

Wrote ps_001 and resolved q_001 in one batch with all 16 assertions, ran tree_correct, and stamped project.updated alone. It explicitly declined the delegation's 'state it as fact', and the next step names question-selection.
Correct ids throughout. The tree_correct batch targeted LR9N-VGQ fact fa26a9c0, R27/F1 and sources S1/S3/S4. No rejections.

Tiered probable, not proved. The reason given is that search_stop is null and the Ashton-under-Lyne nonconformist registers and the Lancashire bishop's transcripts are unsearched; it set shortfall gap and argued those records would corroborate rather than narrow the answer. The narrative keeps conditional language ('The evidence strongly suggests').

Prose with three verbatim-citation footnotes. It describes baptism entry no. 2040 and marriage entry no. 684 with their recorders and the 1832/1833 year discrepancy, and declares the tier. It is readable without the JSON.

It addresses the indexed-1832 vs tree-1833 christening discrepancy. It never mentions that the subject's tree birth fact (24 July 1833, Preston), which the objective restates, falls ten months after the 25 Sep 1832 baptism it relies on. That is an identity-bearing date tension, and the narrative passes over it.

It declared vehicle 'statement' (budget about 150 words), but the narrative runs about 650 words across six sections, with correlation of two records, the maiden-name link and the date-discrepancy reasoning. The declared form does not match the narrative's actual structure.

The ParentChild edges R28/R29 already existed, sourced only to S1, the derivative index; it did not add the original S3/S4 refs to them. Its one primary write marked the Christening fact dated '25 September 1833' as primary even though the original register it cited reads 25 September 1832, so the concluded value on the tree contradicts its own evidence.

Persisted ps_001 at probable/summary/gap with c_001 cited. It added sourced ParentChild R1 and resolved q_001. Its claims about the three sources' classifications and the birthplace resolution match the assertions.

Did everything the delegation asked: ran the gate, concluded, encoded the tree, and stamped project.updated alone. It flagged that the mother is unidentified and that q_001 ('parents') is only partly answered, though it still marked q_001 resolved.
The research_append batch carried the summary then the q_001 update. The tree_edit add_relationship used parent I2 / child I1 with refs S3 (q2), S1 (q1), S2 (q1). All ids correct, no rejections.

The narrative contrasts both neighbouring tiers. It is not proved because exhaustiveness was undeclared, the 1870/1880/1900/1910 censuses and probate are unsearched, and the only direct statement is secondary. It is above possible because three independent originals converge. Shortfall gap matches the named unsearched records.

Self-contained prose. Each record gets its own paragraph with a full citation in italics, an evidence classification and informant analysis, followed by the birthplace resolution and the tier declaration. The src_ labels sit beside the prose descriptions.
Covers both censuses, the death certificate and the derivative Ancestry index (explicitly given no independent weight). It narrates the resolved c_001 and states that no source names the mother.
A Summary for three cleanly correlating sources with one resolved collateral conflict. The structure (source analysis, conflict resolution, limitations, conclusion) follows that form.
No edge existed before the run. It wrote ParentChild R1 (I2 to I1) with three source refs at qualities reflecting direct-secondary and indirect evidence, and made no unnecessary fact writes.

The persisted narrative says the age-79 constraint 'narrows the probable death window to the second half of 1935', and the user paragraph repeats 'the second half of the year'. The window it computed and wrote to the tree is 26 March to 31 December 1935, so 'second half' is false.

States the negative explicitly (two FamilySearch-indexed searches with spelling variants found no certificate). It presents both indirect sources, names the SD State Archives and the unindexed FamilySearch microfilm as where a certificate could be, resolves q_001, and stamps project.updated alone.
Correct ids throughout. The tree_edit add_fact on I1 carried refs S2 and S1, and the tree_correct update_source calls for S1/S2 used only title/author/url/citation. No rejections.

The probable bounded tier is defensible and the narrative explains why it is not proved. But it set shortfall ceiling while exhaustive_search_summary names unindexed FamilySearch microfilm (browse-only images) as unsearched, and the narrative says both that this microfilm 'remain[s] unsearched' and that 'Research is exhausted within the FamilySearch-accessible scope'.

Prose with full citations inline. It separates what was not found (the certificate) from what was found (the Grave Registration, Find a Grave, and the age calculation). There is a stray 'a_003 encodes this' and log_003/log_004 references, but each is described in words.

All three assertions are discussed. The negative search is stated with both spelling variants, no conflicts existed, and the evidence's limits (unknown informants, no primary death information) are stated plainly.
A Summary correlating two sources plus an age calculation, with no competing candidates. The structure moves through evidence, certificate search, a classification table, then the assessment.

A bounded death encoded at probable: tree_edit add_fact Death on I1 with date '1935 (after 26 March, before 31 December)' verbatim, place Gregory, primary true, and refs S2 (q1) plus S1 (q0). This is the synthesized/bounded write the rubric asks for.

Concluded the 25 Jun 1786 Hamre marriage at probable and resolved q_001. It did NOT complete the project: the project write was fields {} and the diff shows only 'updated' changed, with status still active. That is correct because the delegation lacked the objective-answered line.

Did what §8/§9 require when the line is missing: stamped updated alone and named question-selection as the next step ('the delegation does not contain "no further questions — objective answered" — run question-selection'). The user paragraph's closing sentence matches, and the second-opinion sentence was correctly omitted.

Correct ids throughout. The research_append batch carried the summary then the q_001 update, the tree_edit add_fact targeted relationshipId rel-anders-unna with refs S1, and the project update passed fields {}. No rejections.

Probable on a single derivative index entry carrying primary information. It set shortfall ceiling on the grounds that Norway had no civil registration before 1875, so the church book is the only record type, and it said proved would need two independent originals. Shortfall and narrative agree, and the question's search_stop has empty not_reached.

Self-contained prose with the verbatim citation. It describes the groom, bride (the Urna/Unna variant) and event assertions, and the tree christening/death facts it leans on are named with the note that they carry no linked source entry, as §4 requires.
All three assertions are used, and a_002's christening corroboration is brought in. No conflicts existed, and the single-source, index-only, no-confirmed-image limits are stated plainly.

A Summary for one source whose three assertions need correlating with the bride's name variant explained. Statement would have been the leaner option, but Summary is defensible and the structure follows it.

The Couple edge rel-anders-unna already existed with no facts. It added a Marriage fact F1 (25 Jun 1786, Hamre, primary true, ref S1 quality 1) via tree_edit add_fact. This matches the rubric because no evidence fact for the marriage existed beforehand.
